subject.title: Cron Jobs Calendar View for Control UI

question: Should OpenClaw accept a repaired 24-hour Cron Jobs timeline as the first core Control UI slice, or require the broader daily/week calendar and rescheduling design before implementation?
rationale: The remaining work is a new Control UI product surface, the open PR implements only part of the request and is conflicting, and current main has no existing calendar/timeline contract to treat this as a strict bug fix.

options.title: Repair Narrow Timeline First
options.body: Rebase or replace the linked PR onto the current ui/src/pages/cron architecture and accept a scheduler-accurate 24-hour timeline as a first slice while tracking broader day/week/editing scope separately.

options.title: Design Full Calendar Scope
options.body: Pause implementation until maintainers define the daily, weekly, heatmap, popup, validator, and drag-and-drop rescheduling behavior as one product plan.

options.title: Decline Core Calendar View
options.body: Keep the current list/run-history UI as the core surface and close this issue plus the linked PR if maintainers decide a calendar view is not wanted in core.

recommendation.title: Repair Narrow Timeline First
recommendation.body: Rebase or replace the linked PR onto the current ui/src/pages/cron architecture and accept a scheduler-accurate 24-hour timeline as a first slice while tracking broader day/week/editing scope separately.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest current Cron Jobs page product-surface history and likely routing signal for deciding whether to accept a narrow timeline slice.
